correctness.rationale: The cyclic-generator recursion is necessary and sufficient in arbitrary characteristic; the a1=0 branch is a leading-column rank calculation. For a1 nonzero, the quotient action is invertible and kernel lies in the truncated ideal; a recursive gauge conjugates Euler-plus-multiplication to residue-zero terms. The p-curvature operator identity follows from commutators and the cyclic action on set partitions. The first nonzero resonance determines zero-residue nilpotent multiplication kernel, and distinct successive Frobenius constraints fix new coefficients independently. Boundary cases z=0, z=1 and arbitrary finite extension fields are covered. Reproducible exhaustive tests: 25,695 derivations in 29 cases and 96,988 individual tests; finite tests are not an infinite proof.
